metadata.evidence:
A range of green detection
algorithms were tested including ExG (excess green 2g - r - b, developed by Woebbecke et al. 1995), a hue, saturation
and value (HSV) threshold and a combined ExG + HSV algorithm.
metadata.reason: Names the core detection methods implemented by the artifact.

metadata.value: Raspberry Pi HQ Camera + latest software: recall of 74.8% at 5 km/h and 50.5% at 30 km/h; global shutter Arducam AR0234: recall up to 95.7% at 5 km/h
metadata.normalized_value: Raspberry Pi HQ Camera + latest software: recall of 74.8% at 5 km/h and 50.5% at 30 km/h; global shutter Arducam AR0234: recall up to 95.7% at 5 km/h
metadata.evidence:
The
current Raspberry Pi HQ Camera + latest software combination provided a recall of 74.8% at 5 km/h and 50.5 % at 30 km/h.
Recall of up to 95.7% at 5 km/h was achieved by the global shutter Arducam AR0234.
metadata.reason: Quantitative benchmark results for the artifact's detection performance.

metadata.value: up to 120 FPS at the default 416 x 320 resolution (Raspberry Pi 5); recommended 640 x 480 for Raspberry Pi 5
metadata.normalized_value: up to 120 FPS at the default 416 x 320 resolution (Raspberry Pi 5); recommended 640 x 480 for Raspberry Pi 5
metadata.evidence:
Only the Raspberry Pi 5 is currently capable of operating on larger image sizes. Frame rates of up to 120 FPS were recorded at the
default 416 x 320 resolution. We recommend increasing resolution to 640 x 480 for the Raspberry Pi 5.
metadata.reason: Performance characteristic relevant to real-time operation and configuration.
